1.explanation_en: 在位 is the predicate “hold the throne”; 时 makes that state the time setting for what follows.
死 is “die,” and 后 marks the time after that event.
受限制 means “be subject to restrictions”: 受 expresses undergoing or being affected by 限制, “restriction.” 不 negates the whole predicate.
卷 means “sweep or carry along,” and 走 is a directional complement meaning “away.” Together they describe carrying something off from its position.
光和 is the complete reign-era name; 元年, which follows, means its first year.
下 means ‘send down’ and 诏 is an imperial edict; together, 下诏 describes sending out an edict.
被 marks the subject as receiving the action, while 称为 means ‘call as’; together they introduce the name given to the group.
做 (verb, “do/act as”) combines with the role noun 内应 (“inside agent”) to describe the role someone takes on.
约 means “arrange” or “agree on”; resultative 好 indicates that the arrangement is settled. 起事日期 remains separate as what they settled on.
杀 is “kill”; attached aspect particle 了 marks the killing as a completed event. The object 他 remains separate.

1.meaning_en: wrap or put on as an attached covering
1.explanation_en: 裹 is the verb “wrap”; 上 is a result complement indicating that the covering becomes attached. The following 黄巾 is what is put on.
发布 means “issue”; the aspect particle 了 marks the issuing as a completed event. 招军榜, which follows, is what was issued.

1.meaning_en: brought forth; led to the appearance of
1.explanation_en: 引 means “draw” or “bring,” and 出 marks emergence. Together they describe the proclamation bringing Liu Bei into the story; 了 marks the event as completed.
看 means “look,” and unstressed 去 marks the viewing perspective here; it does not indicate movement away.
们 is a plural suffix attached to a person noun; here it makes 孩子 plural.
交 means “form a friendship” here, and attached 了 marks the event as completed; the friends are named separately afterward.
看 means “look,” and 着 marks the looking as ongoing; 招军榜 is the object that follows.
赶 is the verb ‘hurry’; 进 is a directional complement showing movement inward. 城 is the place entered and remains outside this unit.
杀 is the verb ‘kill’; 了 marks the killing as a completed event in this account.
逃难 means fleeing hardship or danger; 了 marks the episode, which is then measured by 五六年. Here 难 is hardship or danger, not the adjective 难 ‘difficult’.
听 means ‘hear’; 后 follows the event to place what follows it afterward. It marks a time relation, rather than meaning ‘behind’ here.
开 is the verb ‘bloom’; 得 introduces the degree complement 正盛, which describes the blossoms’ especially full state.
结为 is a construction meaning ‘form or become as’; 兄弟 names the resulting relationship. Here it describes taking on brotherhood, without specifying more than that.
备 is ‘prepare’; 好 is a result complement meaning the preparation is successfully completed. Together they mean to get something ready.
带 is ‘bring/carry’; 着 is a neutral-tone aspect marker that presents the carrying as an accompanying state. The object伙伴 remains separate.
到 is the verb “arrive”; 了 marks the event as completed here.
出 expresses movement outward, and 阵 refers to a battle formation or battle line; together they describe going out to the fighting.
斩 is “cut”; 成 marks the resulting state, connecting the cutting to what the target becomes. 两段 remains separate.
取得 means “obtain” or “achieve”; the attached 了 marks the event as completed. 第一次胜利 remains a separate object.
被 marks a passive construction, making the subject the one acted upon; 杀 supplies the action “kill.” 后 remains separate, marking the time after the killing.

1.meaning_en: be unable to hold or defend
1.explanation_en: 守 is the verb “defend/hold”; 不住 is a potential complement marking that the action cannot be sustained or achieved. The adverb 快 and clause-final 了 remain outside.
到 means “arrive,” and the attached 了 marks the arrival as completed. 救军 remains separate as the subject.
打 is “fight”; 不 negates the potential result 过 (“overcome”), expressing inability to prevail against the opponent.
听 means listen or heed, and 命 here means orders. Together, the phrase means carrying out the orders, not merely hearing them.
约 means arrange, and 好 is a result complement showing the arrangement is settled. The object 时间 follows separately.
刮 is the wind’s blowing; 起 marks the onset of that event, so together they describe wind starting to blow.
放 is the verb “set off” or “let loose,” and 火 is the noun “fire”; together they form the compact expression for starting a fire.
攻 means “attack,” while 入 supplies the direction “into.” 入 is a directional complement to the attack predicate; the camp location follows separately.
带 means “bring” or “lead,” and 着 marks the accompanying state: Cao Cao arrives with the soldiers along with him. The soldiers remain the separate object.
Here 打 means “carry” or “hold,” not “hit”; 着 marks the resulting ongoing state, describing the flags as being held or carried. 红旗 remains the separate object.
定 is the verb “establish,” and 下 is a result complement: together they present something as set in place. Here it is used of establishing a prohibition.
受到 (undergo or receive) combines with 处罚 (punishment) to express that someone is subjected to punishment; it describes what happens to the person rather than their carrying out the punishment.
获得 means “obtain,” and the attached aspect marker 了 presents the obtaining as an achieved event. It does not mean “now possess” by itself.
带 means “bring” or “take along”; the attached 着 marks the carrying or accompanying as an ongoing state while Liu Bei arrives with the others.
赶 means “hurry,” and 去 is a directional complement indicating movement away toward a destination. The destination is not stated in this clause.
听 is the verb “hear”; 后 follows the verb to make a time expression meaning “after hearing.” Here 后 marks what comes afterward, not a place behind something.
失去 means “lose”; the aspect particle 了 marks the loss as realized, leading into the statement that they no longer have this support.
同意 is the verb “agree”; attached 了 presents the agreement as a completed event before the next clause.
不到 literally means “not reach”; with a time amount, it marks a duration that falls short of that amount.

1.meaning_en: be written on; bear the words
1.explanation_en: 写 means “write”; 着 presents the resulting written state as continuing, so the flag bears the quoted words.
冲 gives the forceful manner of movement; 下山 supplies the downward route, with 山 naming the terrain.
退 means retreat, and the attached aspect marker 了 presents that retreat as a completed event.
救 means rescue; resultative 下 marks successfully securing the person, not movement downward.
冒 means incur or brave, and 着 marks this as an ongoing circumstance while they rescue him.
活 means live; directional complement 下来 here conveys continuing through the danger into a surviving state, not downward movement.
留下 combines 留 (“leave”) with resultative 下 (“behind”); attached 了 presents leaving suspense as an achieved event. 悬念 remains the object.
